name: Metal bracelet watch band

lead: A metal bracelet is a watch band built from articulated links, most often in stainless steel. It is one of the main strap choices for a wristwatch, alongside leather, rubber and fabric.

People choose it for a sharper, more formal or sporty look that holds up to daily wear and water. Because it sits on the wrist all day, it is part of the overall outfit and can be swapped for other straps with spring bars.

paras: The strap is sized by adding or removing links or pins, and closed with a folding clasp, some with micro-adjustment holes or a diver's extension. Common constructions include folded link, pushpin and screw-in styles, plus mesh or Milanese weaves.
Fit matters: loose bracelets slide and tight ones are uncomfortable. Some people react to nickel in steel alloys. Plated versions can wear over time.

chain: Metal links sit visibly on the wrist
Polished, structured look that matches outfit
angle.text: A bracelet adds a finished, metallic accent to the wrist and can be chosen to match other metals in an outfit. It can be resized or changed for another strap.

lead: A metal bracelet watch band is a strap of articulated metal links, typically stainless steel, attached to the watch case by spring bars and closed with a deployant (folding) clasp.[1] Styles include folded-link, pushpin and screw-in bracelets, as well as mesh and Milanese weaves; some are plated with precious metals and a few are made of them.[1]

In style terms, it is how people give a watch a polished, durable and slightly dressier or sportier presence than leather or fabric. Diving-watch bracelets may add extension sections so they fit over a wetsuit.[1] Because spring bars hold them on, bracelets can be swapped with other straps to change an outfit's look.[1]
infobox: Stainless steel, sometimes plated or precious metal

paras: Metal watch straps are commonly stainless steel and come as folded-link, pushpin or screw-in bracelets, with mesh and Milanese braided versions also in steel.[1] Expanding bracelets use springs in a segmented design to slip on like a bangle.[1] Some hybrids pair metal links with silicone contact surfaces.[1]
Deployant clasps often include micro-adjustment holes for fine length changes, and some have a diver's extension.[1] Spring bars let the strap be removed and replaced.[1]
